answer: Opal Pulse Gating: each identity gets a fixed slot in a shared heartbeat clock; its requests must land as one smooth pulse within that slot, measured by inter-arrival variance. Slots that burst then idle are throttled and lose queue priority. Creating convincing traffic shape costs an attacker a continuously staffed client per identity, since padding must track real timing; a falcon-like burst pattern is rejected outright. This raises per-identity overhead to persistent compute and attention rather than a one-time fee.
